title: Debug a tiny page with evidence
goal: Ask for a minimal repair, then compare actual browser rendering.
explanation: Browsers often repair broken HTML, so “it looks fine” is not proof that markup is correct. Do not run unfamiliar scripts. This exercise uses a harmless text-formatting fragment and a sandboxed preview with scripting disabled. Keep the fix small enough to explain each tag.
sampleInput:
Broken fragment:

Welcome builder

Try one small experiment.

Desired: only the word “builder” is strongly emphasized; the second paragraph should not inherit emphasis.
prompt: Find the unmatched formatting element in this HTML fragment. Return a minimal corrected fragment and a short explanation of the repair. Do not add JavaScript, external links, libraries or unrelated styling. Explain why browser error recovery can make the broken result appear inconsistent.
workedExample:
Corrected:

Welcome builder

Try one small experiment.

. The closing strong tag belongs before the first paragraph closes. Browser recovery is not a reliable substitute for a valid structure.

steps.title: Write the expected appearance
steps.text: Specify exactly which word should be emphasized before viewing the model’s answer.

steps.title: Ask for a minimal patch
steps.text: Compare the returned fragment with the original; reject unrelated additions.

steps.title: Preview safely
steps.text: Use the activity’s script-disabled preview or a plain local HTML file containing only this fragment.

steps.title: Check a second case
steps.text: Replace strong with em and repeat the missing-close test. Explain the same structural issue.

steps.title: Teach back the fix
steps.text: Annotate opening/closing pairs and describe why a browser might hide the original mistake.

checks: The corrected fragment closes the intended element at the correct point.
No script, library or external resource is introduced by the repair.
You compare actual rendering and can explain the matched tag pair.
commonMistakes: Running arbitrary generated code because it is labelled a fix.
Accepting a large rewrite that hides the original issue.
offline: Print the snippet and draw lines between opening and closing tags, then sketch the expected rendering.
reflection: Why can a browser display something useful even when the HTML is malformed?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. The corrected fragment closes the intended element at the correct point.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. No script, library or external resource is introduced by the repair.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Running arbitrary generated code because it is labelled a fix.
